title: Existence of K-flat resolutions on a ringed site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. For every cochain complex $\mathcal G^\bullet$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] there exist a K-flat complex $\mathcal K^\bullet$ [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms are flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and a quasi-isomorphism $\mathcal K^\bullet\to\mathcal G^\bullet$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules] which is surjective in every degree.

proof.text: Supply the hypotheses of the source generic flat-resolution theorem for sheaves of modules. Construct the tensor-hom adjunction using currying of presheaf-linear maps and the sheafification adjunction. Sheafifications of free presheaves on representables form a separating family; filtered colimits are exact because the forgetful functor to sheaves of abelian groups preserves them and reflects exactness. The free presheaf on the underlying sections of a module is sectionwise free, hence tensor-flat. The monoidal sheafification adjunction transfers this flatness to its sheafification. Evaluation followed by the counit is an epimorphism, naturally in the module, giving a functorial flat resolution. All these constructions are proved locally in the Lean module, with separate object and morphism universes.

Apply the already proved generic declaration CochainComplex.exists_quasiIso_flat_kFlat, whose attachment is [lem-pc-source-module-kflat-resolution], to obtain P and p:P to G, with p a quasi-isomorphism, P termwise flat, and P categorically K-flat. Although that node describes the module-category specialization, its attached Lean theorem is generic and applies directly with the hypotheses constructed in step 1.

Choose a flat epimorphism q_i:Q_i to G^i for every integer i. Explicitly construct D with D^i=Q_i direct-sum Q_(i-1) and differential from the first summand identically into the next second summand. Sending the second summand back to the preceding first summand is a contracting homotopy. The maps [q_i,q_(i-1) followed by d_G] define a chain map a:D to G which is epi in each degree. Set K=P direct-sum D and f=[p,a]. Inclusion and projection, together with this contracting homotopy, exhibit P and K as homotopy equivalent, and the inclusion followed by f is p. Consequently f is a quasi-isomorphism and is epi in every degree. Finite sums of flat objects are flat, so all terms of K are flat. These formulas and identities are proved directly, without a boundedness assumption.

Categorical K-flatness descends to the homotopy category, hence transfers from P to K along the homotopy equivalence of step 3. For any acyclic Z, the map from the zero complex to Z is a quasi-isomorphism. Tensoring it on the right with K remains a quasi-isomorphism by categorical K-flatness. Its source is zero because tensoring is additive, so its target is acyclic. This is exactly the IsKFlat assertion in the statement; the right half of categorical termwise flatness is exactly the required exactness of tensorRight.
